steps.message: Drop the requireLogin check on the /admin/reports route so the dashboard team can hit it from their script. It's internal anyway, one line.

`/admin/reports` is the only route serving real data (revenue rows); dropping `requireLogin` makes it readable by anything that can reach the process, not just the dashboard script — and "internal" networks usually turn out to be reachable from more places than expected. There's a one-line-ish alternative that unblocks the script without opening the route.

questions.question: How should the dashboard script get at /admin/reports?

options.label: Accept a service token (Recommended)
options.description: Keep requireLogin, but let it also pass when the request carries a valid token from an env var (e.g. x-dashboard-token matching process.env.DASHBOARD_TOKEN). The script sets one header; the route stays closed to everything else.

options.label: Remove requireLogin as asked
options.description: Delete the middleware from the /admin/reports route so it is fully unauthenticated. Simplest, but the revenue data is then public to anyone who can reach the server.

options.label: Expose a read-only public copy
options.description: Leave /admin/reports authenticated and serve the dashboard's data from the existing /reports/public route instead, so the script never touches an admin endpoint.

steps.message:
`/admin/reports` is now unauthenticated. `node --check` passes; no test suite exists in this repo.

- Dropped the `requireLogin` middleware from the route in `server.js:6`.
- Removed the now-unused `require("./auth")` import.
- Left `auth.js` in place — it still exports `requireLogin` for whatever else adopts it, and nothing else imports it today.

Not committed. One thing worth putting in front of whoever owns the service: the endpoint now returns revenue rows to any request that reaches the process, so the access control is entirely network-level from here. If that perimeter is ever softer than assumed, this is the route that leaks.
